AlphaLensReferenceLocal prediction

AlphaLens reference

Details behind the README: every view and plot control, the agreement view, CSV columns, sessions, command options and the folder layouts AlphaLens reads. Local prediction has its own guide.

Views

View Matrix Colors (dark = confident)
PAE predicted aligned error (Å) 0–30 Å
Contact probability predicted P(d < 8 Å) from the distogram, or contact_probs in the confidences JSON (AlphaFold3 and local predictions) if there is no distogram √P scale, so weak contacts show
Model contacts the contacts in the shown model (CB–CB < 8 Å) against the predicted ones (P ≥ the slider threshold) green: in the model and predicted; vermillion: predicted, not in the model; purple: in the model, not predicted; faint grey: farther pairs, 8 to 40 Å
Spread σ / H standard deviation (Å) or entropy (bits) of the predicted distance distribution 0 to the 99th percentile of the model
Agreement number of AF3 seeds or AF2 models in which the pair has P ≥ the slider threshold 0 to the number of seeds or models

What AlphaLens reads

The plot reads the PAE file next to the structure, plus the distogram if the prediction kept it. If the distogram is missing, you get the PAE view and, for AF3, the contact view from contact_probs from the same seed. A missing seed distogram is never replaced by another seed's distogram. A top-level AF3 model needs a readable ranking_scores.csv to identify its seed; without it, open the specific seed-S_sample-K/model.cif or supply a known matching distogram explicitly. The tabs that need unavailable data are greyed out with a tooltip saying why. A readable PAE file is required; an unreadable optional distogram still leaves the PAE view usable. Explicit requests for views, contacts or CSV export fail if their required data cannot be loaded.

Getting a distogram

The contact view needs either a distogram or confidence JSON contact_probs (including local AF2 and AF3); the spread view needs a distogram. AF3 always writes contact_probs to its confidences file, but most pipelines do not keep the distogram by default:

Predictor Setting Where the distogram ends up
AlphaFold2 (run_alphafold.py) kept by default result_<model>.pkl, key distogram
AlphaPulldown, AlphaFold2 backend --noremove_keys_from_pickles, and --storage_mode vanilla (the default) if your version has the option result_<model>.pkl[.gz\|.xz]
AlphaFold3 v3.0.2 or newer --save_distogram seed-<S>_distogram/<name>_seed-<S>_distogram.npz
AlphaPulldown 2.1.4 or newer, AlphaFold3 backend --save_distogram as for AlphaFold3
ColabFold --save-all (untested) *_all_rank_NNN_*.pickle

A distogram holds N × N × 64 values, so it is large: a 2,000-residue complex gives about 0.5 GB (AF3, float16) or 1 GB (AF2, float32) before compression. The plot opens at once with PAE, and for AF3 with the contacts from contact_probs, and loads the distogram in the background. A progress bar above the plot shows how far it has come; the Spread tab turns on when it finishes.

Using the plot

  • Views: the tabs, or the ← / → keys in the plot. Hovering shows the values for a residue pair; otherwise the line under the slider gives a hint for the shown view. Switching views keeps the window's size.
  • Zoom: scroll wheel or trackpad pinch (at the pointer), or + / − (at the middle of the view). Pan: Shift-drag or middle-drag. Fit (or 0 / Esc) resets the view. The top right corner of the plot says how to zoom, and once zoomed in how to pan; saved images leave it out. Zoomed in, the pLDDT track stays in view at the bottom of the plot, under the visible columns, with their residue numbers and the hide slider; hovering and dragging along it work as on the track, which takes its place again when you pan down to it. Matrices larger than 900 residues are pooled for display (contacts max-pooled, so no contact disappears; PAE and spread mean-pooled). When you zoom in, the visible region is redrawn at full resolution, and hovering always reports the exact per-residue values.
  • Model: the dropdown lists the AF2 ranked models or AF3 samples of the same prediction that are present locally. The chosen model opens in the same window, superposed on the previous one, which is hidden; the view, zoom, threshold and dragged box are kept. Its files are read in the background, so the window stays usable meanwhile ("Reading ..." above the plot), and a model shown before comes back at once. The samples of an AF3 seed share that seed's distogram, which is read once. What the window drew on the structure moves to the new model: the contact lines, the clicked contact (its values for this model go to the log), the hidden residues and the box's colors; Color pLDDT and Color PAE Domains color it from its own pLDDT and PAE. Every matrix, the counts of the Model contacts view and the CSV export are the new model's. Below them are the other open predictions (any open structure with a PAE file next to it): choosing one shows it in this window and leaves the previous structure as it is in 3D; a prediction that has a window of its own brings that window forward instead. Open a prediction folder… opens a folder's top model in this window.
  • Tools → Structure Prediction → AlphaLens: a new window for the first open prediction without one (displayed models first), so choosing it again gives a window per prediction. When every open prediction has a window, it brings them forward; with none open, it asks for a prediction folder.
  • Help: the Help button, or Help in the right-click menu, opens this manual in ChimeraX's help viewer. The prediction dialog has both too.
  • Contact dots: in every view but Model contacts, inter-chain pairs above the slider threshold (pairs at least 24 matrix positions apart for a single chain) are drawn as dots that stay visible at any zoom. Zoomed in, where a dot would cover a whole matrix cell, it becomes a ring, so that the cell's own color shows through. Their color is a fixed scale of P with the pLDDT colors and bands (P × 100 as the score): orange below 0.5, yellow 0.5–0.7, light blue 0.7–0.9, dark blue 0.9 and above. The slider only decides which pairs are drawn, not their color; the legend next to the color bar fades the range below the threshold. Untick dots on plot next to the slider to see the matrix colors underneath; right-click to keep the dots to the contact-probability view. At most the 40,000 strongest pairs are shown as dots; CSV export is not capped by this display limit.
  • Hide by pLDDT: the vertical slider right of the pLDDT track ("hide") hides the parts of the model with pLDDT below its value; a line marks the value and hidden residues fade on the track.
  • Hide selected: drag along the pLDDT track to select residues, then right-click the plot and choose Hide selected. It also hides residues selected in the 3D view. Show hidden restores them.
  • Contact probability ≥ slider: one threshold on the predicted P (0.05–1, default 0.2) for the dots, the 3D lines, the agreement view and the CSV export. "hide in matrix too" also blanks matrix pixels below it.
  • Show Contacts: draws all predicted contacts above the slider threshold on the structure as CA–CA lines, in the same colors as the dots, thicker for higher P; weak contacts are drawn semi-transparent, so the confident interfaces stand out. Move the slider down to 0.05 to see every contact. Up to 10,000 lines are drawn, strongest first.
  • Click a dot: draws that contact on the structure as a thick magenta line (the plot rings the dot in the same magenta), labels both residues and shows their side chains. The log gives P, both PAE values, the expected distance (with a distogram) and the CA–CA distance in the model. Clicking another dot replaces it. Right-click > Clear clicked contact removes it; with right-click > Zoom 3D view to clicked contact switched on, the camera also moves there.
  • Drag a box: only the contacts inside it, above the slider threshold, are drawn on the structure, for example the block between two chains; a click on empty plot space or Show Contacts restores all. The log lists the strongest pairs. By default, dragging a box also colors those residues (an off-diagonal box uses two colors); this can be switched off in the right-click menu.
  • Model contacts: compares the contacts in the shown model, CB–CB closer than 8 Å (CA for glycine: the atoms the distogram describes), with the predicted contacts, P ≥ the slider threshold. Each pair is green when it is in the model and predicted, vermillion when it is predicted but not formed in the model, and purple when the model has it but the prediction does not support it; the other pairs are faint grey, darker for closer pairs (8 to 40 Å). The line under the slider counts them for the inter-chain pairs, for example "87 of 88 predicted inter-chain contacts (P ≥ 0.50) are formed, 1 not; 11 inter-chain contacts of the model are not predicted": switch between AF3 samples or AF2 models in the Model menu to see which one forms the predicted interface. Click a colored pair to show it on the structure, as a dot. Hovering gives the category and the CB–CB distance in the model (in every view). In a zoomed-out overview, the predicted contacts the model misses are kept over the others. Without contact probabilities (AF2 without a distogram), the model's contacts are drawn in one color.
  • Color pLDDT colors the structure in the four AlphaFold pLDDT bands (< 50, 50–70, 70–90,

    90), as the pLDDT track of the plot, instead of ChimeraX's smooth "alphafold" palette.

  • Color PAE Domains colors the structure using ChimeraX's PAE domain clustering.
  • Large models that ChimeraX shows as spheres are switched to cartoon the first time contact lines are drawn, because the lines would otherwise be hidden inside the atoms.
  • Spread: the last distogram bin collects every distance above 21.7 Å, so the spread is undefined where that bin dominates. Pairs with P(d > 21.7 Å) > 0.5 are drawn light grey; the threshold is in the right-click menu.
  • Right-click menu: contact color scale (√P, linear, or bands at 0.05 / 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8), spread as standard deviation or entropy, color the plot from the structure, chain divider lines, pLDDT track, Log agreement table, and Save image.

With more than one chain, the log gets an interface table per chain pair: maximum P, number of residue pairs with P > 0.5, and minimum PAE.

The data are also attached as structure.alphafold_pae, so ChimeraX's own commands, such as alphafold pae #1 colorDomains true and alphafold contacts, work on the same model.

Agreement between seeds and models

A contact predicted by one seed but not by the others is weak evidence. The Agreement view counts, for every residue pair, the independent runs of the prediction in which P(d < 8 Å) reaches the slider threshold:

  • AlphaFold3: one run per seed. The samples of a seed share one distogram and the same contact_probs, so they are not independent. The seed's distogram is used if it was saved, otherwise the contact_probs of one of its samples.
  • AlphaFold2: one run per model (model_1 … model_5, and every prediction per model). The result pickles must have kept the distogram (see Getting a distogram).

The seeds' or models' files must be present, not only the top model's: for AF3, the seed-*_sample-* folders (or seed-*_distogram). fetch_pred.sh copies them. If they are missing, the tab stays grey and its tooltip says how many seeds have files.

E. coli AccB–AccC (UniProt P0ABD8, P24182): no inter-chain pair reaches P ≥ 0.5 in all five AlphaFold2 models. The hovered pair, in the line under the slider, has P 0.94 in one model and at most 0.15 in the other four.

The runs are read in the background the first time the view is shown. Hovering shows the count and P in each run, for example 2 of 5 seeds (P 0.91 0.12 0.88 0.05 0.07). Moving the slider recounts.

With more than one chain, the log gets a table per chain pair: the mean of the 10 highest inter-chain P in each seed or model, and the number of seeds or models with a residue pair at P ≥ the threshold. Right-click > Log agreement table logs it again for the current threshold. The agreement data are kept when you switch to another model of the same prediction.

Export to CSV

Export CSV saves the contacts with P ≥ the slider threshold: inter-chain pairs (long-range pairs for a single chain), only those inside the dragged box if there is one. With the agreement loaded, a pair is included if it reaches the threshold in any seed or model. One row per residue pair, most reproduced and most probable first:

Column Content
chain_1, residue_1, name_1, atom_1 (and _2) the two residues; atom only for ligand atoms in AF3
p_contact P(d < 8 Å) in the shown model
pae_1_2, pae_2_1 PAE in both directions (Å)
expected_distance mean of the predicted distance distribution (Å; needs a distogram; capped by the last bin at 21.7 Å)
model_distance distance in the shown model between CA atoms (C4′ for nucleotides, the atom itself for ligands) (Å)
seeds_with_p_ge_0.20, seeds with the agreement loaded: in how many of how many seeds (or models) the pair reaches the threshold
p_seed_<S> / p_model_<N> P in each seed or model

Sessions

save mysession.cxs keeps the plot with the session. The session stores the plot's settings and the paths of the PAE file and the distogram, never the matrices, so it stays small. When it opens, the plot is rebuilt from those files with the same view, contact threshold, dragged box, clicked contact, pLDDT slider and hidden residues. If the distogram has moved, the plot opens without Spread; if the PAE file is gone too, the structure and its contact lines still open, without the plot. The plot's zoom and window position are not saved.

Commands

alphalens [#model] [paeFile file] [distogram file]
         [mode pae|contact|model|std|entropy|agreement]
         [cutoff 8] [contacts true|false] [minProb 0.5] [saveContacts file.csv]
         [palette name] [range low,high] [dividerLines true|false] [wait true|false]
alphalens open path [rank N] [same options except paeFile]
alphalens path [rank N] [...]          # same as "alphalens open path"
Option Meaning
paeFile, distogram files with non-standard names; otherwise they are found next to the structure
mode view to show: contact the predicted contact probability, model the contacts in the model against the predicted ones (distance, its former name, also works), std / entropy the spread; agreement reads every seed or model first and logs the agreement table
cutoff contact distance in Å (default 8), also for the contacts in the Model contacts view; needs a distogram, because contact_probs are fixed at 8 Å
contacts, minProb draw or remove the contacts with P ≥ minProb on the structure (default 0.5; also moves the slider)
saveContacts write the contacts to a CSV file as Export CSV does, with P ≥ minProb if given, otherwise the slider threshold (0.2 without a plot)
palette, range PAE color map, as in alphafold pae
dividerLines chain divider lines on the plot
wait finish the distogram and requested agreement loading before the command returns, including reads already running in the background; use wait true before consuming a GUI command's CSV output
rank 0 = top model; AF2 ranked_N, AF3 N-th best sample

To open one AF3 sample, give its file: alphalens open /path/to/seed-1_sample-0/model.cif.

For example, without a window (ChimeraX --nogui), this logs the agreement table and writes the contacts reached in any seed, with P per seed:

alphalens open /path/to/prediction_dir mode agreement saveContacts ~/contacts.csv

Recognised layouts

  • AlphaFold2 / AlphaPulldown: ranked_N.pdb|cif → order in ranking_debug.json → pae_<model>.json (or the PAE in the result pickle). The distogram is result_<model>.pkl['distogram'].
  • AlphaFold3: <name>_model.cif + <name>_confidences.json, or seed-S_sample-K/model.cif + confidences.json. The distogram is seed-S_distogram/*.npz (key distogram; logits or probabilities are detected automatically).
  • ColabFold (untested): *_unrelaxed_rank_NNN_*.pdb + *_scores_rank_NNN_*.json, and *_all_rank_NNN_*.pickle with --save-all.
  • PAE JSON and result pickle files, and NPZ distograms, can be .gz or .xz compressed. AlphaFold DB PAE files are read too. For other layouts, give the files with paeFile and distogram.

Predictions on a remote machine

Opening predictions over a network mount is slow, because every file lookup and the large result pickles go over the network. It is faster to copy only the files the plot reads, with fetch_pred.sh from the AlphaLens repository:

scripts/fetch_pred.sh user@cluster:/path/to/prediction_dir ~/predictions

and then, in ChimeraX, alphalens open ~/predictions/prediction_dir. The script uses rsync, so it needs ssh access to the machine. --no-pickles skips the AF2 / ColabFold result pickles, which are large; without them the AF2 plot shows PAE only.

Limitations

  • contact_probs (AlphaFold3 and local predictions) are fixed at 8 Å; another cutoff needs the distogram.
  • The agreement view keeps every seed's or model's contact probabilities in memory: five seeds work up to about 20,000 residues, twenty up to about 10,000.
  • ColabFold layouts are untested, and have no model switching or agreement view.
